Claude said: 
> Every surface uses ToLocalTime(); RestaurantOptions.ResolveTimeZone() has no caller and the container sets no TZ, so a deployed instance shows guests UTC. I kept the existing convention here rather than putting two time formats on one screen — the static header and the island are one page. The fix needs a decision §13 never made (12- vs 24-hour), so it wants its own slice before M5.

The UTC convention is impractical. 
While internally, it makes sense to store events in UTC, 
we know a restaurant has a physical location 
which has an IANA time zone 
Looks like §13 has 
| `RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE` | `America/New_York` | rendering only |
which we should use to render any date and time in the application. 
For example, lets say the restaurant is in Asia/Tokyo and a customer is away in America/New York 
the customer logs into the website to see past orders. what time zone should we display? 
my decision is the user's local time zone is irrelevant. We should always display and render all date time
in restaurant time zone 
which now adds a new requirement. 
the website footer should show the current date time accurate to the second and ticking continuously 
on every single page on the website 
in restaurant time zone
when we refresh the page, 
this clock should update from the server 
but for normal operation, I think once we have the datetime from the server we can trust the local computer clock to keep it up to date. 
you may use performance dot now or similar technology to keep the clock in sync 
always keep in mind that not just the look and style should be mindful of responsive mobile design 
but also the performance should be mindful that most users will be on a phone or similar handheld device 
so the web browser or operating system could do things to save battery 
please fix and also there is an error in the razor 
and remember to update documentation when changing code

The build error: TableOrderSurface.razor:350 calls LinesFor(entry.GuestOrderIdentifier), which was never written. _partyLines was loaded in LoadAsync and then read by nothing.

F-36's true extent: 18 call sites across 10 Razor files, all .ToLocalTime(). ResolveTimeZone() genuinely has no caller.

The design decisions I made
Restaurant time, always — your ruling, encoded as: nothing outside one class may call ToLocalTime(). New MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Time.RestaurantTime is that class, with Time / TimeWithSeconds / Date / DateAndTime / DateAndTimeWithSeconds / MachineReadable, all formatted with explicit patterns under InvariantCulture — the same trap MoneyText already documents for "C".

The 12-vs-24 question §13 never answered — new RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT, default 12-hour, validated at startup. Non-required so no existing RestaurantOptions construction breaks.

The footer clock, no server timer. A per-second Blazor timer would tick only on interactive pages, cost a circuit message per second per tab, and keep a phone's radio awake. Instead the footer renders one anchor (instant + offset + when the offset next changes, precomputed and memoized) and js/clock.js advances it locally: setTimeout aimed at the next second boundary, fully cleared on visibilitychange, one string compare before any DOM write, contain: content + tabular-nums so the tick can't reflow the page.

Elapsed time comes from performance.now(), but it's cross-checked against Date.now() every tick — because performance.now() stops on several platforms while a device is suspended, which is precisely the phone-in-a-pocket case. Divergence triggers a re-anchor from a new anonymous GET /restaurant-clock, which also covers the table display living on one URL for days and any page open across a DST boundary. That endpoint is exempted from the obligations pipeline alongside /healthz.

State of the tree
Done and staged: RestaurantTime.cs, RestaurantClockEndpoints.cs, RestaurantClockFooter.razor, clock.js, both layouts, App.razor, _Imports.razor, app.css, RestaurantOptions.cs, Program.cs, ObligationsEnforcement.cs, all 18 call sites, and the LinesFor fix (as a grouped lookup built in LoadAsync, not a query per diner).

Not yet written: RestaurantTimeTests.cs (I'd verified the fixtures — 2026-07-26T19:04:05Z → Sun 26 Jul 2026, 3:04:05 PM, offset −240, next transition 2026-11-01T06:00:00Z → −300), the RestaurantOptionsTests and ObligationsEnforcementTests additions, .env.example / compose.yaml / run.sh, and the docs — S§13, a new S§11.7, R§8, closing F-36 in DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, and docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m4-slice-3.md.

Done
Extracts at the repo root — 32 files, 6 new and 26 changed. Nothing to delete.

The build fix
LinesFor never existed; _partyLines was loaded and read by nothing. Rather than reinstate a .Where() scan per bill entry, LoadAsync groups the one sitting-wide read into _partyLinesByOrder and LinesFor is a dictionary lookup — §11.1 renders a row per person, so a query inside that loop would turn a six-person table into six extra round trips on every §9 notification.

F-36, closed
Your ruling is stronger than the spec was, and I encoded it that way: not "prefer the restaurant's zone" but the reader's zone is irrelevant. All 18 ToLocalTime() call sites now go through one type, Time/RestaurantTime.cs, and nothing else may call it — the only surviving mention in the tree is the doc comment forbidding it.

The entangled locale question is now RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT (12-hour default, 24-hour), validated at startup so a typo fails the process rather than quietly showing the wrong clock everywhere. It's deliberately not required, so IdentityWiringTests.BuildOptions() and friends keep compiling.

The footer clock
No server-side timer. A Blazor timer would tick only on the interactive half of the surfaces and cost a circuit message per second per tab. The component renders one anchor, pins ShouldRender() => false, and clock.js takes over: setTimeout aimed at the second boundary, timer cleared on visibilitychange rather than fired-and-ignored, one string compare before any DOM write, tabular-nums + contain: content so a tick can't reflow the page.

Two things I added beyond the brief, both because of surfaces that outlive a page load:

The next DST transition ships in the anchor (bisected to the second, memoized), so a page open across 1 November stops rendering EDT without a reload.
GET /restaurant-clock — anonymous, no-store, exempt from the obligations pipeline. performance.now() is monotonic but stops during device suspend on several platforms, so a phone in a pocket for an hour wakes an hour behind. Both clocks are read each tick and a >2s divergence triggers a re-anchor. Also every 10 min visible, and on resume after ≥1 min hidden. Never while hidden, never more than once a minute, failures ignored.
I verified in Node that the JS formatters are byte-identical to the C# invariant patterns across 12/24-hour, midnight/noon, and a 45-minute offset (Asia/Kathmandu) — otherwise the handover at page load shows as a flicker.

Worth knowing
DisplayLayout now wraps @Body in .display-main and is a column — the card is still centred, but check it on the tablet since that's a real layout change. And the culture-independence test mutates ambient culture inside using scopes; if you see cross-test flakiness in the web test assembly, that's the first place to look.
